The STR-encoder contains an embedding layer and N multi-head self-attention layers divided into two blocks: the first N-K layers capture context information (shared across tasks), while the last K layers use task-specific MASK matrices (MASK^ner for NER, MASK^rc for RC) to focus attention on task-relevant words. The NER and RC losses are summed (L = L_ner + L_rc) and backpropagated jointly through the shared STR-encoder, allowing the shared layers to learn joint features between entity and relation types.
